name: Michael J. Allen

summary.text: Michael J. Allen is the elected district attorney for Colorado's 4th Judicial District (El Paso and Teller counties), elected in 2020 and reelected in 2024.
He is the Republican nominee for Colorado attorney general in 2026, having defeated David Willson 59.9%-40.1% in the June 30 primary.

experience.text: Served in the U.S. Navy from 1991 to 1998 as an Aviation Electronics Technician.
Bachelor's degree from the University of Northern Colorado (2001) and law degree from the University of Kansas School of Law (2005).

Worked as a prosecutor in Kansas, including in the Kansas Attorney General's Office's consumer protection division, before returning to Colorado as a deputy district attorney in the 4th Judicial District.

record.title: Created an Organized Crime Unit targeting fentanyl trafficking
record.detail: His campaign says the unit, targeting fentanyl traffickers, drug cartels and violent robbery rings, 'has prosecuted more fentanyl-death cases than any other office in Colorado, and secured the longest prison sentences statewide' (exact date not given on the page; bounded to the start of his tenure as DA).

record.title: Prosecuted the Club Q mass shooting as a hate crime
record.detail: Secured what his campaign describes as the second-longest prison sentence in Colorado history (exact date not given on the page; bounded to the start of his tenure as DA).

record.title: Launched Colorado's first motor vehicle theft team
record.detail: His campaign says the team helped cut motor vehicle theft in the district by 50% in 2025.

record.title: Publicly called for felony fentanyl-possession penalty after Commerce City deaths
record.detail: Issued a public statement calling on the governor and legislature to raise fentanyl possession back to a felony and add a mandatory sentencing enhancer for distribution deaths, after five people died of a suspected fentanyl overdose in Commerce City.

positions.source_title: Michael J. Allen — iVoterGuide Candidate Profile
positions.quote: Human life deserves legal protection from conception until natural death.
positions.note: iVoterGuide does not show an exact response date; the survey appears to have been completed before the June 30, 2026 primary candidate deadline. He also said an elective abortion should be allowed only for a medical emergency.

positions.quote: This rating accurately reflects your support for the Second Amendment and your commitment to defending the right to self-defense for Colorado residents.
positions.note: From an NRA Political Victory Fund letter posted on his own campaign site, giving him an 'AQ' rating (the highest given to non-incumbents) for the 2026 primary; exact letter date not shown.

positions.quote: Our members will see your 'AQ' rating as a sign that you are a strong supporter of gun rights and hunting, advocating for the Right to Keep and Bear Arms.
positions.note: NRA-PVF letter praises general support for 'gun rights and hunting,' not a direct statement on Amendment 83's constitutional hunting-rights measure specifically.

positions.source_title: Michael Allen, Jena Griswold: Colorado attorney general election voter guide
positions.quote: the law already gives us the ability to work with federal agencies when there's criminal elements involved, and I think it's probably fine the way it is now. I'm not sure that we need a ballot measure on that.
positions.note: Declined to take a position on the ballot measure itself ('that's up to the voters') while suggesting current law may already be adequate — coded as a mixed/middle position.

positions.source_title: Calls to address deadly fentanyl epidemic in Colorado increase following tragedy in Commerce City
positions.quote: The first step should be increasing the penalty for possession of fentanyl back to a felony because as little as 2mg of fentanyl can be deadly.
positions.note: Statement made in 2022, predating Proposition 132 on the 2026 ballot, but calling for the same change (felony for any amount, plus a mandatory sentence enhancer for distribution deaths).

research_notes: A Colorado Sun / Noticias Univision debate between Allen and Griswold was scheduled for 6:30pm MDT on Oct. 14, 2026 (the day this research was done); no recap was available yet, so worth checking for a post-debate article before publishing. Could not source Allen's position on child-trafficking sentencing (Prop 133), public lands, federal tariffs/budget law, or state tax measures (Amendment 87/Prop 136/Prop NN) despite searching — these are less central to an AG race but left unknown rather than guessed. An opinion column (coloradopolitics.com, 'Michael Allen can't be trusted on ICE,' Oct. 2, 2026) attributes a quote to Allen from a radio interview praising an ICE officer's conduct in a fatal shooting; this was not used to code any position because it is reported secondhand through a hostile opinion piece rather than a neutral source — flagged for a reviewer to independently verify if needed. The domain michaelforag.com, which appears in some search results as a Michael Allen gun-issues page, actually resolves to a lapsed site for a different candidate (Michael Dougherty) and was not used.
